field_conventions.cbm_edge: UPPERCASE_SNAKE_CASE identifier from CBM analyzer output (e.g., 'HTTP_CALLS', 'HANDLES')
field_conventions.dr_relationship: predicate name from predicates.json or null if unmappable
field_conventions.usage: edge classification: 'verification_and_mapping' for edges that create DR relationships, 'traversal_only' for edges used as evidence, provenance or traversal input; implementation_note says why an edge is traversal-only, and names the catalog addition it waits on when that is the reason
field_conventions.dr_scope: scope of the relationship (intra-layer, cross-layer, both)
field_conventions.direction: relationship direction (forward, backward, bidirectional, or caller_to_callee)
field_conventions.confidence_from_property: code property that determines confidence level (e.g., visibility, export status)
field_conventions.dr_pattern: '<source layer.type> → <destination layer.type>' of the DR relationship, after directionality_transform; for verification_and_mapping edges it must name a triple in the relationship catalog
field_conventions.order: the first mapping is the call-graph default edge type, so CALLS comes first
field_conventions.conditions: for verification_and_mapping edges: predicates lists, in order of preference, the predicates that can express the edge ({predicate, invert}; invert when the DR relationship runs from the CBM edge's target to its source). The relationship is the first catalog triple that exists between the two classified element types (cli/src/analyzers/edge-relationships.ts); dr_relationship, directionality_transform and dr_pattern describe one listed preference and a typical case. 'gate' says what else must hold

mappings.description: A function calls another function: the caller depends on the callee
mappings.implementation_note: Listed first: it is the call-graph default edge type for dr analyzer callers and callees. Creates a relationship only between functions that both survive classification.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

mappings.description: A function or method handles an HTTP route: the API operation for that route realizes the application function
mappings.implementation_note: CBM writes the edge handler → Route; the DR relationship runs from the operation to the function it realizes (api.operation.realizes.application.applicationfunction), so the direction is inverted. HANDLES names routes by path while Route nodes are named __route__METHOD__/path.

mappings.description: A class defines a method: the application component is assigned the application function
mappings.implementation_note: Deterministic. Map only when both ends survive Tier-1 classification as these types. A controller class (application interface) defining handler methods (API operations) becomes api.operation uses application.applicationinterface, the catalog's triple for that pair.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

mappings.description: Module or file import dependency: one application component uses another
mappings.implementation_note: Map only between modules both classified as application components; imports of external packages, and of anything else, stay traversal input (datastore detection reads them).

mappings.description: A callable is used as a value (handler or callback registration): the registering function depends on it
mappings.implementation_note: Same treatment as CALLS.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

mappings.description: An argument flows into a parameter: data flows from the calling function to the called one
mappings.implementation_note: Documented by CBM, not observed in the eval corpora.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

mappings.description: A function or component uses a data structure without calling it: it accesses the data object
mappings.implementation_note: The largest-reach edge (387 gold cards). Map only when the target was accepted as a data object (an Interface, Type, Enum or data class); usage of variables and anything else is traversal only. CBM rates USAGE as identifier use without a proven target, so confidence is low. A data-model object schema used by a function or component is the provider: data-model.objectschema serves the user (inverted).

conditions.gate: target accepted as a data structure (application.dataobject, data-model or api schema); usage of plain variables is traversal only

mappings.description: A function or component mutates a data structure's state: it accesses the data object
mappings.implementation_note: Same triples as USAGE; only when the written variable or field belongs to an accepted data object.

mappings.description: A class implements an interface that was classified as an application interface: the component provides that interface
mappings.implementation_note: Only when the implemented interface was accepted as application.applicationinterface. Implementing a data-object interface creates no relationship (the catalog has no component-to-dataobject structural triple, by design).

mappings.description: A test function exercises a symbol: the test case sketch tests that function, interface, service or operation
mappings.implementation_note: Requires the separate test pass (inventory step 7): test code is excluded from the main candidates by filtering_rules, so test functions are classified on their own as testing.testcasesketch.

mappings.description: A test file covers a source file: the coverage target tests the component
mappings.implementation_note: File-level counterpart of TESTS; same test pass.

mappings.description: A function publishes to a queue or topic: it depends on the application event the queue carries
mappings.implementation_note: The queue or topic Route (__route__sqs__..., __route__kafka__...) is modelled as an application event. The 'triggers' reading from a function or component waits on catalog addition 3.

mappings.description: A function listens on a channel: it depends on the application event
mappings.implementation_note: Function-level listeners. The interface-level reading waits on catalog addition 4.

mappings.description: Code starts an external program: the system software serves the calling component
mappings.implementation_note: Inverted: CBM writes caller → Process, the catalog has technology.systemsoftware.serves.application.applicationcomponent. Documented by CBM, not observed in the eval corpora.

mappings.description: Infrastructure dependency between artifacts (charts, packages, base images) or system software
mappings.implementation_note: Infrastructure only in CBM 0.10.2 (charts, package files, base images, compose depends_on).

mappings.description: A Kubernetes Service selects workloads: each workload node realizes the technology service
mappings.implementation_note: Inverted: CBM writes Service → workload. Needs the infrastructure pass (Resource nodes).

mappings.description: Manifests, charts or Terraform are deployed onto a cluster: the node composes the artifact
mappings.implementation_note: Inverted: CBM writes artifact → cluster. Needs the infrastructure pass.

mappings.description: Outbound HTTP call from code to an API route
mappings.implementation_note: Blocked on a catalog addition: no relationship from an application type to api.operation expresses a consumer calling an operation. proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

mappings.description: Outbound gRPC call
mappings.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

mappings.description: Outbound GraphQL call
mappings.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS; in the binary and UI only. proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

mappings.description: Outbound tRPC call
mappings.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS; in the binary and UI only. proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

mappings.description: Class or interface inheritance
mappings.implementation_note: specializes between components and between data objects; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 1); map once accepted.

mappings.description: Class or interface extension
mappings.implementation_note: Present in the CBM 0.10.2 binary only, not in its documented vocabulary or any observed graph; kept for forward compatibility. INHERITS is the edge CBM emits for class extension.

mappings.description: Method override
mappings.implementation_note: specializes between functions; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 2); map once accepted. Also Kustomize patches in infrastructure.

mappings.description: A function emits on a channel
mappings.implementation_note: triggers an application event from a function or component; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 3); map once accepted.

mappings.description: A function raises an exception class
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence for error-handling concerns; triggers an application event when the exception is a domain event, proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 3); map once accepted.

mappings.description: A method throws an exception class
mappings.implementation_note: Same as RAISES: evidence for error-handling concerns; the triggers reading waits on catalog addition 3.

mappings.description: Folder contains folder
mappings.implementation_note: composes between directory-level components; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 5); map once accepted.

mappings.description: A workload addresses a Service
mappings.implementation_note: depends-on from a node to a technology service; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 9); map once accepted.

mappings.description: A file defines a symbol
mappings.implementation_note: Provenance: supplies source_reference.file for every element mapped from a symbol. Not a relationship between elements.

mappings.description: A decorator applies to a symbol
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence: decorator names feed the Tier-0 rules (extraction-heuristics.json) and the card. Decorator is not an element.

mappings.description: A symbol reads a config key, or a config key names a symbol
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence for security and APM concerns (EnvVar is not an element).

mappings.description: Folder contains file
mappings.implementation_note: Traversal only: the directory structure behind placement facts.

mappings.description: Package containment
mappings.implementation_note: Binary and graph UI only; treat as CONTAINS_FOLDER if emitted.

mappings.description: Membership
mappings.implementation_note: Binary and graph UI only; treat as DEFINES if emitted.

mappings.description: Resolved call
mappings.implementation_note: Binary and graph UI only; treat as CALLS if emitted.

mappings.description: Vocabulary-mismatch similarity (score >= 0.80)
mappings.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; for Tier-0 clustering and duplicate detection.

mappings.description: MinHash near-clone
mappings.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; for duplicate detection.

mappings.description: Files that change together in history
mappings.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; evidence for component boundaries.

mappings.description: Git branch metadata
mappings.implementation_note: Provenance for source_reference; not a relationship.

mappings.description: Documentation references a file
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence for descriptions and for Tier 2's upper-layer inference.

mappings.description: Documentation mentions a symbol
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence for descriptions and for Tier 2's upper-layer inference.

mappings.description: Cross-repository call or channel
mappings.implementation_note: These are DR's qualified cross-model references (@model/layer.type.name in a references field), not relationships inside one model; mapped when federated extraction is built.
